cards.front: When describing people, when do you use SER vs. ESTAR?
cards.back:
SER — permanent or inherent traits: identity, nationality, personality, physical features considered fixed.
ESTAR — temporary states: current mood, temporary condition, how someone looks right now.
cards.grammarNote: The line is not always sharp, but a helpful rule: ser for WHO someone is, estar for HOW someone is right now.

cards.back:
yo soy
tú eres
él/ella/usted es
nosotros somos
vosotros sois
ellos/ellas/ustedes son
cards.grammarNote: Ser is highly irregular — each form must be memorized separately.

cards.back:
yo estoy
tú estás
él/ella/usted está
nosotros estamos
vosotros estáis
ellos/ellas/ustedes están
cards.grammarNote: Estar is mostly regular but has stress accents on all forms except nosotros/vosotros.
Ser is used for beauty as a fixed, defining trait. Es muy guapa — this is who she is.

cards.back: Ella está muy guapa esta noche.
cards.grammarNote: Estar is used when you mean 'she looks beautiful right now' — a temporary observation. Esta noche (tonight) reinforces the temporary context.

cards.front: She is funny and very kind.
cards.back: Ella es divertida y muy amable.
cards.grammarNote: Personality traits use ser — they describe who she is at her core, not just how she is acting right now.
Estar for emotional/physical states — nervousness is temporary. Esta noche (tonight) makes the temporary nature clear.
Nationality always uses ser — it is a defining characteristic. Colombiana is feminine, agreeing with ella.

cards.front: I am tired after dancing all night.
cards.back: Estoy cansado después de bailar toda la noche.
cards.grammarNote: Estar for physical states — being tired is temporary. Después de + infinitive = after doing something.

cards.back: Eres muy encantador. (m.) / Eres muy encantadora. (f.)
cards.grammarNote: Ser for personality — being charming is a stable trait. The adjective changes ending for gender.

cards.front: I am so excited for this concert!
cards.grammarNote: Estar for emotional states — excitement is temporary. Emocionado (m.) / Emocionada (f.) — the adjective agrees with the subject.
Ser is used when you are characterizing or defining a place — this is what the bar is like as a whole.

cards.front: The bar is packed tonight. (current state)
cards.back: El bar está lleno esta noche.
cards.grammarNote: Estar for current conditions — lleno (full/packed) describes a temporary, observable state.

cards.front: What is the difference? Eres guapa. / Estás guapa.
cards.back:
Eres guapa — You are beautiful. (a permanent, inherent quality; a defining compliment)
Estás guapa — You look beautiful. (right now, tonight; a compliment on how she looks at this moment)
cards.grammarNote: Both are compliments, but estás guapa is often used when someone has dressed up or looks especially good for the occasion.

cards.front: Fill in: She ___ very fun (personality), but tonight she ___ tired.
cards.back: Ella es muy divertida, pero esta noche está cansada.
cards.grammarNote: Es (ser) — divertida is a personality trait (permanent). Está (estar) — cansada is a temporary physical state.
